result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.get_assortativity()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Calculate assortativity for numeric node attributes. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L29227-L29316){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.get_assortativity(attribute) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Numeric assortativity](/assets/graphs/get-assortativity.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Two triangles joined by one edge, each node shaded by a numeric attribute shown in its badge: 1, 2, 3 on the left and 7, 8, 9 on the right. Low values link to low and high to high, so the correlation across edges is positive, r = 0.774." width="100%"} Measures the tendency of nodes with similar numeric attribute values to connect. Returns the Pearson correlation coefficient of attribute values across edges, indicating whether similar values tend to be connected. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [attribute]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Name of the numeric node attribute to analyze. Must exist on all nodes and be convertible to float. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Assortativity coefficient in range `[-1, 1]`: - `r = 1`: perfect positive correlation (identical values connect) - `r > 0`: assortative (similar values prefer to connect) - `r = 0`: no correlation - `r < 0`: disassortative (dissimilar values prefer to connect) - `r = -1`: perfect negative correlation ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If attribute doesn't exist on all nodes, isn't numeric, graph has no edges, or attribute has no variance. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} For a numeric attribute this reduces to the Pearson correlation between the two endpoint values across every edge. Positive coefficients pick up homophily on the numeric axis (collaborators with similar publication counts, friends of similar ages), while negative coefficients flag structural pairings that link dissimilar values, such as mentor-mentee edges in academic networks or price-inversely-related pairs in economic graphs. The metric assumes the attribute has non-zero variance across nodes (a constant attribute produces a $0/0$ division and raises `ValueError`), and it is sensitive to outliers, so running the same computation on log-transformed or rank-transformed values is a common robustness check. ## Examples {.doc-examples} When people mostly befriend others close to their own age, connecting similar numeric values, the numeric assortativity comes out positive: ::: {#6a22f6c8 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec g = ( ec.Graph(directed=False) .add_node("Alice", age=25) .add_node("Bob", age=27) .add_node("Carol", age=26) .add_node("Dave", age=55) .add_node("Eve", age=53) .add_edge("Alice", "Bob") # Similar ages (25-27) .add_edge("Bob", "Carol") # Similar ages (27-26) .add_edge("Dave", "Eve") # Similar ages (55-53) .add_edge("Alice", "Carol") # Similar ages (25-26) ) # Returns a positive value: similar-aged people tend to connect g.get_assortativity("age") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 0.9915397631133672 ``` ::: ::: In academic mentorship networks, senior researchers often collaborate with junior ones, connecting dissimilar values and producing a negative coefficient: ::: {#a7d8675e .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} g = ( ec.Graph(directed=False) .add_node("Junior1", papers=5) .add_node("Junior2", papers=7) .add_node("Senior1", papers=50) .add_node("Senior2", papers=45) .add_edge("Senior1", "Junior1") .add_edge("Senior1", "Junior2") .add_edge("Senior2", "Junior1") ) # Returns a negative value: experienced researchers connect to juniors g.get_assortativity("papers") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` -0.9905454545454547 ``` ::: :::
